newsitem.title: USA: S. Dakota lawmakers okay gas tax hike for flood.
newsitem.headline: S. Dakota lawmakers okay gas tax hike for flood.

text.p: South Dakota legislators early Tuesday approved a temporary gasoline tax increase to raise $24 million for flood damage repairs, the spokesman for Gov. William Janklow said.
In a special session that concluded shortly after midnight, legislators approved a 3 cent per gallon tax increase for a 17-month period beginning May 1, spokesman Jim Soyer said.
Proceeds from the tax hike were to go to repair state and local roads that have sustained flood damage, Soyer said.
As of noon Monday, the flood had been reported to have caused an estimated $24 million of damage to state highways, $22 million in counties and another $7.5 million to township roads, Soyer said.
That "snapshot" damage estimate will likely rise as the state receives more reports, Soyer said.
The legislation has been forwarded to Janklow, who had proposed a 2 cent increase when opening the session on Monday night.
